title: The trace-formula local Frobenius agrees with the geometric-point local Frobenius
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\neq p$, and the coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: a finite extension $E/\Ql$ inside $\Qlb$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$ and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $K=(M,\theta)$ be an $E$-Weil complex [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], with $\theta:Lg_\gamma^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ for the geometric-Frobenius automorphism $g_\gamma=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$. Let $K_{\mathcal O}$ be a lattice of $M$ whose reductions $K_{\mathcal O}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n$ lie in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$ of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] for all $n\geq1$, as in [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model], and take $\varphi_E=\theta$ there.

Let $x\in|X_0|$ be a closed point [def-weil-closed-points] with residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field] and degree $e=[\kappa(x):k_0]$. Choose a $k_0$-embedding $\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow k$; let $\bar x:s\to X$ be the associated geometric point and $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^e})$ the rational point it represents. Write $F^{\mathrm{trf}}_x=F_{y,e}$ for the $E$-stage local operator of [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] on the stalk complex $K_{E,\bar x}=K_{\mathcal O,\bar x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$. Write $F_x$ for the local operator of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] on $C_{\bar x}=\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*M)$, formed with the same $\bar x$.

Then for every $j\in\mathbf Z$ there is an $E$-linear isomorphism
$$\mathrm H^j(K_{E,\bar x})\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm H^j(C_{\bar x})$$
carrying $\mathrm H^j(F^{\mathrm{trf}}_x)$ to $F_x$. In particular, for every $j$,
$$\det\bigl(1-T^eF^{\mathrm{trf}}_x\mid\mathrm H^j(K_{E,\bar x})\bigr)=\det\bigl(1-T^eF_x\mid\mathrm H^j(C_{\bar x})\bigr)\quad\text{in }E[T],$$
and the same identities hold after scalar extension along $E\subset\Qlb$.
